get.description:
Stages, what each needs, what has been uploaded, and the pending/rejected
submission — 409 execution_not_started before the signed agreement.

post.description:
One execution photo (a slot from photo_slots) or document (a type from
document_types). Replaces the earlier file in that slot/type; a submission that
already used the earlier one keeps it.

get.description:
A short-lived signed link to one execution file — the owner (a territory viewer
only when territory_viewers_see_documents is on). Every link is audited.

post.description:
Submit an execution stage for Grid Nova to check. Its evidence must already be
uploaded; text evidence (references, serials) comes in `text`.
All or nothing: any bad row saves none, and every bad row is listed.

get.description:
Instant duplicate check. Another project's details are shown only when that
project is one you can already see.

post.description:
Upload one checklist document or one site photo. The server records when it
received the file; GPS and the client's capture time are stored if supplied.
Photos record their provenance (app/execution/photos.py): `capture_method` camera
(GPS + captured_at required) or gallery (phone gallery; location optional).
`accuracy_m` (photos): the GPS fix's reported accuracy, stored and returned as-is —
a camera photo's fix can then become the site location (POST .../site-location).

get.description:
A short-lived signed link to one uploaded file — the owner (a territory viewer
only when territory_viewers_see_documents is on). Every link is audited.

The latest formal proposal for this customer, if Grid Nova has prepared one —
with a download link once it is approved, so it can be delivered in person. A
territory viewer sees its status only: no price (money is owner-only) and no PDF
unless territory_viewers_see_documents is on.
The handover checklist, the warranty register (once handed over) and the PDF state.

A short-lived signed URL for the handover PDF — the owner (a territory viewer only
when territory_viewers_see_documents is on).

post.description: Cancel a payment you recorded, while it is still `recorded`.
A screenshot or scan (JPEG/PNG/WEBP/PDF, ≤ 10 MB) proving the payment.

get.description: The project's sales progress, stage by stage (anyone who can view the customer).

post.description:
Record that the approved formal proposal was handed over and accepted in person
(owner only). The alternative to the customer's online accept link.

Ask Grid Nova to prepare the FORMAL proposal (owner only; needs the approved site
assessment). Creates no draft — staff prepare it. Says whether the customer record
has everything a formal proposal needs.

The owning associate raises a request for their customer (multipart; up to
service.max_photos images in `files`). 409 not_handed_over before the handover.

Set the customer's site location (owner only; draft/submitted — a submitted
customer returns to draft, like any edit). One fix per call: phone GPS, a camera
photo's GPS fix (recommended), a Google Maps link, or pasted coordinates. The new
location is UNCONFIRMED until POST .../site-location/confirm.

The associate confirms the location is the customer's house (required to submit,
even for a precise GPS fix). 409 site_location_not_set when there is none.

Declare the customer's record complete (every required document uploaded) so
staff can make the verification call.

get.description:
Which survey sections are complete (and what each still needs), the two
signatures and the customer's declaration.
Every correction request for this customer, newest first.

post.description:
Ask Grid Nova to change survey fields of a VERIFIED customer (draft and
submitted customers are edited directly). Owner only; one pending request at a time.

get.description:
A short-lived signed link to the survey report — a document: the owner (a
territory viewer only when territory_viewers_see_documents is on). Audited.

Sizes, the suggested size and its limiting factor, the indicative list price for
both packages with the subsidy, and warning codes — on the saved data.

post.description:
One on-screen signature (multipart: `file`, a PNG). The customer's also needs
`declaration_name` (the name the customer typed) and `customer_confirms_data=true`.
Owner only; draft or submitted (a submitted customer returns to draft) — or a
verified customer whose signature an applied survey correction cleared.

get.description:
Grid Nova's own account, for the "pay only here" reminder. Withheld while the
account details are still placeholders — never show a customer a dummy account.
The caller's payouts in approved or paid batches, newest month first.
The caller's Associate ID and the share path, so the frontend never builds it.
The caller's own referred enquiries, newest first.

Every associate in the caller's territory below the caller's level, with how
many customers each has onboarded. Preferred Associates only (403 otherwise).
Counts cover all of a member's customers; a customer an Admin closed after an
attribution conflict is not counted.

post.description:
One customer message → Nova's reply. A plain function on purpose: the agent
and the model client are synchronous, so FastAPI runs this in its threadpool and
a slow reply never holds up any other request.

get.description:
BE-19: the active Admins, so "ask an Admin" can name them. Any staff member;
`email` only for a viewer who is an Admin (null otherwise).

Which roles receive each staff alert, and whether each currently reaches anyone.
Any staff member sees counts; a viewer with staff.manage also gets `addresses` (BE-19).

Every role × permission with labels and descriptions (config/access_control.yaml)
— the "Who can do what" page. Any staff member.

Last 15 audit entries as a human-readable feed (all roles). Engineers do not
see pricing-related entries, matching the dashboard's pricing-visibility rule.
Anyone who does not see every lead (Sales) only sees entries that trace back to
a lead they can access; entries about no lead at all (employees, equipment,
governance) are left out for them.

Requests you asked for, or that you could decide (BE-19: a staff change only when
you may assign every role it touches). `{items: [...]}`, newest first; each item
carries `requested_by_name`.

post.description: Apply the change, re-checked with your permissions. You cannot approve your own.
Withdraw your own pending request.

Validate a template CSV (dry_run=true, the default — nothing is written) or write
its accepted rows (dry_run=false with the `batch_token` the dry run returned, which is
the file's SHA-256). Rows with errors are skipped and listed; warnings are stored with
the row. The same file cannot be imported twice unless the first batch is voided.
Hide every project of the batch from every read path. Nothing is deleted.

get.description:
Newest commissioning first: {items, page, page_size, total}. Filters narrow before
paging, so `total` is the filtered count. `q` searches the Grid Nova ref and, where the
role may see them, customer name, address, block, district and state.

Counts and capacity sums by scheme, state, district and commissioning year, computed
in SQL over the same filters as the list. Unmatched place names are grouped as typed.

The header row and one commented example row (it starts with #, so the importer
ignores it). No real data.

Both programmes, newest first. Same {items, page, page_size, total} shape as
the other paginated dashboard lists. The page and the count come from SQL (one
UNION over both programmes); only the page's applications are loaded.

post.description:
Approve an application under review. Requires the verification call — this
stands in for OTP verification — to be recorded as completed, with a note.

In one transaction: the Associate ID is issued, the associate created and (for a
Preferred Associate) the seat taken. After it commits, on the background runner
(app/jobs/runner.py): the Clerk invitation, the ID card and welcome letter PDFs,
and the notification — so the response does not wait for them. A failure in any of those
is recorded on the associate and retried from the dashboard; the approval stands.

get.description: A short-lived signed link to one uploaded KYC document.

post.description:
submitted → under_review; under_review → needs_info (note required) or
rejected (reason required, as `note`); needs_info → under_review.

Send the associate's Clerk invitation — or send it again: after a failure, or
(BE-19) when the one sent was never accepted (expired, lost, wrong address since
corrected), which revokes the old invitation first. Refused once the associate has
signed in (409 invalid_transition).

get.description:
Admin / Management: the Associate's personal-sale rate today — standard, individual
and effective — every scheduled change, the full history of individual rates (with
the internal reason) and the earliest dates a change may take effect.

post.description:
Admin: set the Associate's individual rate from effective_from (rate_percent null =
back to the standard schedule). A reduction needs the notice period; an increase may
take effect today. A new row every time — nothing is edited. Audited; the
Associate is told (home feed, email) without the reason. With second approval on:
202, applied when a second Admin approves.

get.description:
BE-20: the associate's open customers (all of them with `include_closed=true`), so
staff can choose which to move: [{onboarding_id, client_code, customer_name, status,
project_stage, open}]. The same permission and region rule as reassign-customers.

post.description:
Render and store the ID card and welcome letter again (after a failure, or
once the welcome-letter text has been supplied). The associate ID never changes.

get.description:
Admin / Management: one Associate's customers, verified payments and commission in
a period (IST days, inclusive; default this month so far, at most 366 days) —
app/commissions/performance.py defines each figure.

post.description:
BE-19: move a suspended or deactivated associate's open customers to an active
associate (app/associates/reassignment.py). Both associates must be in the caller's
regions. Audited per customer.

active ⇄ suspended → deactivated. Suspending or deactivating needs a reason.
Deactivation is final and releases the associate's seat; suspension keeps it.

BE-19: after the change commits, Clerk access follows it — suspending or
deactivating bans the associate's Clerk user (every session ends) or revokes an
unaccepted invitation; reinstating unbans. The database refuses a non-active
associate on every request regardless, so a Clerk failure is reported (`access`)
and the change stands. `open_customers` says how many customers still need moving
(POST …/reassign-customers); a suspended associate's commission is frozen.

keep_existing: the earlier onboarding keeps the customer and the later one is
closed. award_new: the later one takes the customer and the earlier one is closed
(its attribution lock ends). Closed records are kept, never deleted.

get.description: Associate queries, oldest due first. `overdue=true`: open and past due.

post.description: Accounts/Admin answer a query (once). The associate sees it on their home feed.

get.description: Every published version, newest first, and which is in force today.

post.description:
Admin: publish a new version (never an edit). Every rate key is required. With
second approval switched on (config/access_control.yaml) this answers 202 and the
schedule is published when a second Admin approves.

Admin, audited: compute every entry still waiting for confirmed rates — at the
schedule in force on its agreement date where that is a real schedule, otherwise
at this (real) schedule.

get.description: The commission ledger, newest first. Dates are IST days on created_at.

post.description:
earned → approved, all or nothing (409 entries_not_approvable lists why each
refused entry cannot be approved).

Admin (policy 4.7): reverse commission obtained through false information or a
breach of the Network Terms. Not yet paid out → a reversal; already in an
approved or paid batch → a recovery from the next payouts.

get.description:
Everything remembered about one customer — the profile, then the raw
memories. This is the audit view: what the agent believes and why.

Admin/Management: who a lead can be assigned to — active employees holding a role
PATCH /leads/{id}/assign accepts (leads.be_assigned: Admin or Sales), name-sorted. Deliberately
minimal (id/name/role only): unlike GET /employees this is not an employee-
management surface, so no email, calendar or activity data is exposed.

Any authenticated employee's own record: the roles and permissions this request
was authorised with (from the database), whether this session completed two-step
verification, and whether any held role needs it. `role` is the primary role.

OAuth callback — identifies the employee from the signed `state` (no bearer on
a browser redirect), exchanges the code, and stores the refresh token encrypted.
Always ends in a 303 back to the dashboard (see _calendar_redirect).

Start the Google OAuth consent flow for the authenticated employee. The `state`
is single-use and expires after 10 minutes (app/scheduling/oauth_state.py).

patch.description:
Deactivate an employee. Never deletes the row — every historical lead,
proposal, meeting and audit-log reference keeps pointing at a real employee.
A deactivated employee is also blocked at sign-in (see
app/auth/dependencies.py) so this actually stops them, not just labels them.

get.description:
What this person leaves behind: open leads, open proposals they drafted, pending
invitations they sent.

patch.description:
Reactivate a previously deactivated employee. Audit-logged like every
other change to an employee's standing.

post.description:
Move every open lead of this person to another employee who takes leads. Needs
staff management and lead assignment.

put.description:
The states a person works in (TerritoryState names); empty = every region. Applied
to Network Manager associate lists (app/auth/scoping.py).

post.description:
Make `role` the person's one role — the pre-BE-17 form of PUT …/roles, with the
same rules (scope, Admin floor, second approval for Admin/Accounts → 202).

put.description:
Replace a person's roles. Only roles you may assign, on people whose roles you may
assign; never your own Admin role; never below the Admin floor. Granting or removing
Admin or Accounts waits for a second Admin (202). Takes effect on their next request.

get.description:
Projects in execution. `needs_attention=true`: a submission awaiting
verification, stuck past its stage's threshold, or a project flag (e.g.
dcr_mismatch). `stage` matches the current (last recorded) stage.

Accounts only: the bank upload file for an approved (or paid) batch — the only
place a full account number leaves the system. Every export is audited.

One row per payout line of the financial year (default: the current one), with
the associate's PAN — decrypted through the audited helper.

What the agents have actually been doing, against what they are allowed to do.

Two counts that matter more than the rest: `denials` (an agent reached for
something governance refused) and `guardrail_blocks` (an agent said something
that had to be withheld). Both should be near zero; a rising number is the
signal to look at, which is the whole reason they are counted separately.

What every AI agent in this system is permitted and forbidden to do.

Served from the registry the enforcement layer actually reads, so this can never
drift from what the agents are really allowed to do — the failure mode of a
governance page maintained by hand.

How the agents are performing: volume, failures, latency and model spend.

Every number is derived from the run records the harness writes, so the report
and the audit trail cannot disagree — the one thing an operations view of an
autonomous system must never do.

post.description:
Admin or INTERNAL_API_KEY (Cloud Scheduler). Emails Accounts once about each open
query past its due time. Idempotent; an overlapping run answers
{"status": "skipped", "reason": "already_running"}.

Admin or INTERNAL_API_KEY. Emails Operations once about each project that has
become stuck at a stage (it is not emailed again for the same stage). Idempotent; an
overlapping run is skipped.

Admin or INTERNAL_API_KEY. Emails Accounts once per overdue milestone and once
per payment left unverified past the threshold. Idempotent; an overlapping run is
skipped. Also retries receipts still pending (app/jobs/sweeper.py): `receipts_retried`.

Admin or INTERNAL_API_KEY (Cloud Scheduler). Emails Operations once about each open
request past its SLA. Idempotent; an overlapping run answers
{"status": "skipped", "reason": "already_running"}.

Admin or INTERNAL_API_KEY. Scans for quiet leads and fires internal follow-up
notifications. Idempotent — safe to call repeatedly (Cloud Scheduler calls it); an
overlapping run answers {"status": "skipped", "reason": "already_running"}. Also
retries proposal PDFs that never finished (app/jobs/sweeper.py): `pdfs_retried`.

Admin or INTERNAL_API_KEY (Cloud Scheduler, gridnova-jobs). Reminds owners of proposals
not opened and about to expire, expires the overdue ones. Idempotent.

Admin or INTERNAL_API_KEY. Emails staff once about each survey that has waited
longer than review_target_hours for its review (not again for the same wait).
Idempotent, also when two runs overlap.

get.description:
A page of leads, newest first: {items, page, page_size, total}. `q` matches the
customer's name, email or phone, or a lead id — for an Engineer (who never sees
contact details) only a lead id. Every filter runs in SQL.
Optional: `stage` (repeatable), `min_score`/`max_score` (low<medium<high), `created_from`/
`created_to` (IST days, inclusive) — see docs/api/staff_contracts.md; `referred_by_associate_id`
(an Associate ID: leads that came through that Associate's referral link — docs/api/associate_ease.md).

post.description:
A staff-entered enquiry (phone call, WhatsApp, walk-in, referral). Creates a
real Customer (deduplicated email-first, then phone), Project (with a reference
ID) and Lead, then evaluates qualification exactly as a manual field edit does.
Sales owns what it enters; Admin/Management leave the lead unassigned.

schema.title: Response Get Lead Api V1 Dashboard Leads  Lead Id  Get

patch.description: Admin/Management: give a lead to (or move it to) an active Admin or Sales employee.

Manual correction/completion of a lead's collected fields — the employee-side
escape hatch for when AI extraction (chat, or its mock-mode heuristic) missed
something or got it wrong. Re-evaluates qualification exactly the way a chat
turn does, so a manually-completed lead becomes just as "qualified" as one
qualified conversationally.

get.description: The shape of GET /onboardings/{id}/payment-schedule, with lead_id.

Milestones, payments (staff view, newest first), totals and the project summary —
the shape of GET /onboardings/{id}/payments, with lead_id. Before acceptance the
schedule is empty and the totals null.

The receipt of one verified payment (staff view) with a short-lived link to its PDF
(`pdf_url`, null while it is held or not rendered yet). The customer's own link is
`url` (the public token route); it stays null while the receipt is held or void.

post.description:
Force a reflection on a lead now, instead of waiting for a milestone.

Synchronous on purpose — the caller asked for it and wants the result, unlike
the automatic path where a customer is waiting on a reply.

Employee-initiated booking — books on a connected calendar after re-verifying
the slot is free (shares book_meeting with the conversational path).

patch.description:
Opportunity tracker: move a lead to any pipeline stage by hand. Marking it
lost, or re-opening a won/lost lead, requires a reason; it is recorded verbatim
in the audit log and on the lead's timeline.

get.description:
All meetings across every lead, newest-first — the Meetings dashboard page's
data source. Same {items, page, page_size, total} shape as GET /audit-log.
Sales sees only meetings on their own connected calendar (matching
can_schedule_meeting()'s own admin/sales split); Admin/Management see every
meeting. Engineers have no reason to see customer-identifying meeting data
(same "nothing to access yet" restriction already applied to their lead view), and
Operations and Accounts see no customer data at all (app/auth/scoping.py).

post.description:
Ask a question about a customer and get an answer from stored memory.

Read-only. The answer is grounded in retrieved records only — whatever is not
on file comes back as not on file, never as a guess.

get.description:
Counts and money for the whole network. The period (IST days, inclusive)
defaults to this month so far and applies to revenue and commission figures.

post.description:
Ask Nova Records a question. `status` is answered | not_on_record |
needs_clarification | refused; every number in `answer` comes from the records and
`tables` are built from the rows (docs/api/nova_records.md).

get.description: The caller's own conversations, most recent first (at most 50, within retention).

One conversation with every turn as it was shown. Own only; Admin may read any for
audit (that read is written to the audit log). Anything else is 404.

post.description:
Admin or INTERNAL_API_KEY (Cloud Scheduler). Deletes conversations last used more
than retention.days ago (NR-3). Idempotent; an overlapping run answers
{"status": "skipped", "reason": "already_running"}.
Was this answer helpful? On the caller's own turns only; sending again replaces it.

get.description:
`needs_attention=true`: every customer whose formal proposal is blocked
(`formal_proposal_blocked` set — requested, but the record lacks what a draft
needs); `false`: everyone else.

post.description:
Generate (or, until it is signed, regenerate) the customer agreement PDF for
printing on ₹10 stamp paper. Needs the customer's acceptance on record.
Upload the signed agreement scan with the stamp paper's number and date.

get.description: The indicative estimates the associate showed this customer (read-only).

post.description:
Operations/Admin add the installed equipment to the catalogue from its nameplate
(model as printed, DCR from the OEM declaration). The brand must be an approved make
for the project's package and component (Grid Nova's master data); otherwise
`equivalent_reason` is required (422 make_not_approved). Returns the catalogue item;
units then reference it by `equipment_id`.

Admin records why a PM Surya Ghar project with a non-DCR module may still claim
the subsidy. Clears the dcr_mismatch flag and the subsidy_claimed block.
Grid Nova's own team uploads execution evidence (grid_nova mode only).
Admin only: Grid Nova takes over this project's execution from the associate.
Operations confirm the register; it is locked from then on.

Operations/Admin match an unmatched unit (registered with the brand/model as
printed) to a catalogue item — of the unit's category and agreeing with its declared
DCR status. Create the item first with POST .../execution/catalogue when it does not
exist. Staff only; associates never see unmatched status.

Record an execution stage directly — projects Grid Nova executes itself. On an
associate-mode project only an Admin may, and only with `admin_override_reason`
(recorded with via `admin_override`, audited).

get.description:
The latest formal proposal for this customer, if Grid Nova has prepared one —
same shape as the associate-facing endpoint.

post.description:
Prepare (draft) the FORMAL proposal — the deliberate, separate step after the
site assessment. Drafts through the usual Proposal Agent; approval tiers, manager
sign-off and the send-guard then apply exactly as for any proposal.

Fix-in-place: `customer_email` fills in a missing email first, in the same call —
for a request blocked on "no email on file".

get.description:
The checklist (computed items and manual ticks), whether it is complete, the
warranty register once handed over, the PDF state and — staff only — the customer
link state (never the token) and email state.

post.description:
Operations / Admin: the customer's acknowledgement — a signature image (PNG, method
`signature`) or an in-person tick (method `in_person`, no file).

Operations / Admin: issue a NEW customer link (any earlier one stops working),
render the PDF if needed and email the customer (unless send_email is false). The link
is returned this once. 409 handover_not_recorded / handover_pdf_held.
Operations / Admin: the customer's link stops working at once.
Operations / Admin: the O&M contact details were (or were not) given to the customer.
Operations / Admin: the customer orientation was (or was not) given.

get.description: A short-lived signed URL for the rendered handover PDF (404 until it exists).

post.description:
Operations / Admin: render the handover PDF again (after the register changed or a
failed render). Runs in the background; poll GET .../handover `pdf.status`.

Hand-record a stage that has no action of its own: `accepted` (the customer
accepted offline) or `portal_agreement_approved` (the customer approved the
Vendor-Consumer Agreement on the PM Surya Ghar portal). A note is required; an
optional reference (e.g. a portal application number) is kept as evidence.
Record that the approved formal proposal was handed over and accepted in person.

get.description: Every service request for one customer, newest first.

post.description:
Operations / Admin / Engineer: raise a request on a customer's behalf (multipart;
up to service.max_photos images in `files`). 409 not_handed_over before handover.

Correct the customer's site location during the verification call (Admin, Sales).
Stored as `staff_entered`, unverified, confirmed by this staff member; a reason is
required and the change is audited with before/after. The status does not change.

get.description: A short-lived signed link to the latest survey report. Every link is audited.

post.description:
Render and store the survey report (after the review). A new call stores a new
file; the earlier one is kept.
Record (or replace) the feasibility review of a complete, signed survey.

The staff verification call. Required before any future commission
eligibility; it also starts the attribution lock.

get.description: The Overview page's four headline counts, each with a prior-day `trend` value.

patch.description:
Adjust a proposal's price BEFORE approval and re-derive the manager-signoff flag.

The flag is recomputed from the Business Rules Engine on every adjustment, with no
way to bypass it — so a price nudged over the threshold always requires manager
sign-off, and one dropped back under correctly reverts to standard approval. Only
permitted while the proposal is still in draft / pending_pricing_validation; a price
change on an approved or sent proposal must go through request-revision instead.

Recent denial and kill-switch history for one agent — who changed what,

Liveness: the process is up. Touches nothing else. `environment` and
`llm_mode` are included only for a caller with a valid X-Internal-Key — they tell
an outsider which deployment (and whether it has a model) they are probing.

Readiness: the database answers, its schema is at this build's Alembic head and —
in production — the territory master is loaded. 503 names the failing check;
nothing about the connection is disclosed. `territories` reports what is loaded.
The result is cached for READINESS_CACHE_SECONDS (0 = never).
